verdict: NOT READY TO MERGE: 2 blocking, 4 major, 3 minor, 5 notes. The production diff is sound at flag OFF for normal model output. Two things block. First, T12 fails in every order, so CI backend-tests goes red. Second, the parse marks are read from the LLM's own JSON, so a response byte can change with every flag OFF. Two more nodes are order-dependent: T6 (already known) and T13 (new). GREEN's T13-attributed kills M08, M24 and M49 were therefore spurious; I re-proved all three. All 16 files are sha-identical at the start and the end. Every mutant was restored and its sha256 matched.

findings.title: T12 is red in every order (CI backend-tests red), and because of it no working repo node protects the Bright Data log hygiene
findings.evidence: adv-g1: tests/test_s75_fanout_starve.py::test_T12 FAILED at :484. The 403 leg is answered 401, so there is 1 ERROR record, not 2. adv-comm-04 (CI order): T12 is the only failure (1 failed / 1375 passed). Root cause: _bd_client (test_s75:185-198) reads httpx.AsyncClient on every call. After the first monkeypatch that attribute is the previous factory, which ignores the new transport. Blast radius: T12 is red with or without a mutant, so it kills nothing. The Bright Data mutants are killed only by notes-folder probes. Mine: B01 (latch keyed on 'any status': a 403 after a 401 is silent), B02 (_AUTH_LAST written only on a status's first rejection), B03 (402 treated as an auth rejection), B04 (zone in the ERROR message). GREEN's: M06, M07, M27, M28, M29. With the helper fixed (GREEN probe_t6_t12.py, re-run as adv-gprobes: 3 passed), B03 and B04 are killed. B01 and B02 are killed by adv_probe.py::test_adv_bd_one_error_per_status and ::test_adv_bd_snapshot_tracks_the_latest_auth_status.
findings.fix: One RED hunk: capture _REAL_ASYNC_CLIENT = httpx.AsyncClient at module scope and use it inside factory (GREEN Q1). Then promote two nodes into the repo: test_adv_bd_one_error_per_status (401,401,403,403 gives exactly 2 ERRORs, status=401 then status=403) and test_adv_bd_snapshot_tracks_the_latest_auth_status (401,403,401,402 gives last_status 401,403,401,401).

findings.title: Flag-OFF response byte moves: _parse_marks honours _parse_presplit / _parse_fallback keys that come from the LLM's own JSON
findings.evidence: parse_product_query returns json.loads(model output) unfiltered (extraction_service.py:1548). _parse_marks (scs ~1818) reads the two keys from any dict, and both entries feed it the LLM result. adv_defects.py ran with every new flag OFF and an LLM stub returning LLM_PARSED plus one key. Result: 2 FAILED (adv-defects0). The partial carries metadata.parse_presplit=true (or parse_fallback=true). The same path flips parser_path to False (A2b escalation) and skips _track_gpt_cost (the parse goes unmetered). The trigger needs the model to emit an underscore key (a user prompt injection or a hallucination), so the practical impact is low. It still breaks FG-10's 'every response byte' claim, which is the rubric's blocking class. GREEN disclosed this as Q3 but left it open.
findings.fix: In _parse_with_budget, on both LLM branches (the bare await and the wait_for), return a copy of the LLM dict without '_parse_presplit' and '_parse_fallback', so that only the presplit and fallback builders can set the marks. This keeps the FG-4 contract, and T14/T17 stay green. Promote adv_defects.py::test_defect_flags_off_llm_supplied_mark_is_not_honoured[both] as a repo node, red first on the current bytes. Add the stream twin.

findings.title: T13 fails SOLO on the GREEN bytes (new; order-dependent like T6), so GREEN's M08 / M24 / M49 kills were spurious
findings.evidence: adv-t13-solo (-k T13, unmutated bytes): FAILED at :524 'brightdata_auth' in body. adv-t12t13 fails the same way. The mechanism: T13 imports app.main inside the node, after the bd_env fixture has set BRIGHTDATA_API_KEY. app/main.py:11 load_dotenv(override=True) then fires the dotenv guard (tests/conftest.py:16-29, install_dotenv_guard), which re-neutralizes credentials. The key is deleted, so bd_search_web returns before any HTTP call and no 401 is recorded; the stdout shows no [brightdata] line at all. T13 passes in file order (T6 imports app.main first) and in CI order (adv-comm-04). GREEN's mutant logs fs-mut-M08, M24 and M49 show the identical :524 failure, so those kills prove nothing. I re-proved them with adv_probe_t13.py, which imports app.main at collection: D08 snapshot never written, D24 /health spread removed and D49 'at' not ISO-UTC were all KILLED (adv-mut-D08-1, D24-1, D49-1).
